t: A republic of 1819–1831 joining Venezuela, New Granada, Quito and Panama, proclaimed by Simón Bolívar’s Congress of Angostura.
Its armies, led by Bolívar and Sucre, ended Spanish rule in South America at Junín and Ayacucho in 1824.
Regional rivalries, debt and disputes over Bolívar’s power broke it into Colombia, Venezuela and Ecuador by 1831.
dyk: Its official name was simply the Republic of Colombia; historians later coined ‘Gran Colombia’ to distinguish it from the present-day country.
ev: Congress of Angostura proclaims the Republic of Colombia after the Battle of Boyacá
Congress of Cúcuta adopts a constitution; the Battle of Carabobo frees Venezuela
Sucre wins the Battle of Pichincha and Quito joins the republic
Colombian armies end Spanish rule in South America at Junín and Ayacucho
José Antonio Páez leads the Cosiata revolt in Venezuela
Bolívar assumes dictatorial powers and survives an assassination attempt
Venezuela and Ecuador secede; Bolívar dies near Santa Marta
The remaining provinces are reorganised as New Granada

f.successor: Republic of New Granada; Venezuela; Ecuador
